personas.name: Dr. Jameela Jamil
personas.tagline: I need AI that can think like a specialist and communicate like a human.

demographics.occupation: Researcher and PhD Program Coordinator at the College of Human and Social Sciences

personas.background: Dr. Jameela Jamil is a highly analytical academic and researcher working as a Researcher and PhD Program Coordinator at the College of Human and Social Sciences. She expects AI systems to do more than provide generic answers, and instead wants them to adopt distinct professional perspectives such as a general user, a specialist, a biologist, or a sustainability expert. She uses LinkedIn and Instagram as part of her professional advocacy work, helping translate scientific research into broader social awareness. She values scientific rigor, but also wants responses to be rewritten in a human-like style that makes academic knowledge more engaging and accessible to the public.
goals: Access responses framed from different expert perspectives
Maintain scientific accuracy in AI-supported outputs
Translate academic research into socially engaging public content
Use AI to bridge technical depth and public awareness
frustrations: AI tools that respond too generally to specialist questions
Outputs that lack scientific nuance or perspective switching
Responses that are accurate but stylistically too robotic for public engagement
Difficulty balancing technical rigor with accessible communication

interaction_preferences: Prefers text for verifying scientific data and citations
Values human-like stylistic rewriting for public-facing outputs
Likes comparing outputs from multiple professional viewpoints
Uses AI iteratively for both accuracy and tone refinement

personas.quote: I'm interested to get the prompts from different perspectives, like what the chatbot knows as a general user and as the specialist, as a biologist... and also as the sustainable scenario.

personas.name: Professor Jeff
personas.tagline: Give me the big picture clearly, privately, and without artificial friction.
personas.background: Professor Jeff is an unconventional thinker, senior academic, and executive leader who values pragmatic insight and broad context over overly guided or bot-driven interactions. He is privacy-conscious and avoids active social media participation because of concerns about data harvesting, manipulation, and loss of autonomy. Although he is critical of many digital platforms, he has a strong preference for audio-based learning and often listens to podcasts at 1.5x or 2x speed so they feel more natural and efficient. He wants AI to support oral information digestion while preserving user control and minimizing robotic delivery.
goals: Absorb big-picture insights quickly and efficiently
Protect personal privacy while using digital tools
Use audio to consume information in a natural, high-speed format
Avoid bot-led questioning that slows down the exchange
frustrations: Social platforms that harvest data and manipulate users
AI systems that ask too many questions instead of providing answers
Robotic or unnatural voice experiences
Interactions that reduce his control over pace and direction

interaction_preferences: Strong preference for audio features
Listens to spoken content at 1.5x to 2x speed
Prefers concise, big-picture delivery
Avoids active social media posting due to privacy concerns

personas.quote: I avoid the social media because I hate the corruption underlying everything... They're harvesting data to manipulate you... I just don't like that much invasion of my privacy.

personas.name: Dr. Bashir
personas.tagline: Turn long documents into useful summaries that save me hours of work.

demographics.occupation: Economist and Researcher at Education Above All

personas.background: Dr. Bashir is an economist and researcher at Education Above All who treats AI as a personal peer, mentor, and productivity partner. His work involves reviewing long and complex documents, and he sees significant value in using AI to summarize 20- to 30-page materials into concise, digestible outputs. He is professionally active, uses LinkedIn for networking, and is especially interested in tools that can reduce manual effort while improving daily workflow. He also values speech-to-text and text-to-speech integration as part of a larger vision for continuous knowledge enhancement and research support.
goals: Summarize long documents into digestible insights
Reduce hours of manual reading and synthesis
Use AI as a personal peer for daily productivity
Integrate audio and text workflows into research practice
frustrations: Manual review of lengthy documents that takes too much time
AI tools that fail to extract the core message accurately
Workflows that separate summarization from speech capabilities
Systems that are not practical for day-to-day professional use

interaction_preferences: Prefers text for reviewing extracted summaries
Values speech-to-text and text-to-speech integration
Uses AI as a professional assistant and thought partner
Wants concise outputs that can immediately support work tasks

personas.quote: I would love to use this one for my day to day work... extracting information from a 20 or 30 page document which takes two hours of my time... and use this tool to extract a summary.

personas.name: Professor Habib
personas.tagline: I value friendly AI, but only when it stays accurate and text-based enough to verify.
personas.background: Professor Habib is a highly technical academic who prioritizes correctness, validation, and alignment with trusted learning materials. As a physics professor and researcher, he approaches AI with the expectation that it should simplify difficult concepts without sacrificing scientific reliability. His social media use is limited, and he mainly relies on professional channels to disseminate his research. He finds text to be the most natural and dependable way to learn and verify information, though he appreciates AI interactions that feel friendly and realistic when explaining complex mechanisms.
goals: Verify explanations against trusted learning materials
Use AI to clarify complex scientific mechanisms
Maintain depth and correctness in technical learning
Rely on text for careful review and validation
frustrations: Audio-only formats that move too fast for technical depth
Simplified explanations that reduce scientific accuracy
Systems that feel engaging but are hard to verify
Interfaces that do not support careful text-based checking

interaction_preferences: Strongly prefers text for deep learning and verification
Uses AI to simplify technical ideas while preserving correctness
Appreciates friendly and realistic interaction styles
Relies on text as the primary learning modality

personas.quote: For me, [text is] something very natural... this is the old fashioned and then the best way of learning and performing... although it's very easy to read here, but okay, a text is better.

personas.name: Dean Marcus
personas.tagline: The best educational AI combines engagement, accessibility, and multimodal learning.
personas.background: Dean Marcus is a senior university leader who thinks about technology in terms of educational impact across a wide range of stakeholders. He is especially interested in how AI can support students with learning disabilities and enable more personalized learning pathways. His experience makes him attentive to the engagement quality of educational materials, and he is critical of monotone or flat audio experiences. He prefers multimodal interaction, particularly formats that combine listening with synchronized reading, because the dual input helps him focus and stay engaged.
goals: Support more personalized learning paths for students
Improve accessibility for learners with different needs
Use AI to communicate effectively with diverse university stakeholders
Promote multimodal educational experiences that improve focus
frustrations: Monotone audio that fails to engage learners
Single-mode content that does not support different learning needs
Educational tools that ignore accessibility concerns
Experiences that do not sustain attention or focus

interaction_preferences: Prefers multimodal experiences combining audio and text
Values synchronized reading while listening
Evaluates tools through accessibility and engagement
Looks for learning experiences that improve focus
accessibility_needs: Values features that support learners with disabilities and different learning preferences

personas.quote: I prefer the audio podcast. If the podcast didn't have the writing as you go, like reading as you go, I wouldn't prefer it... because I hear it and I read it, I'm choosing it.
